I am Zhang, 67 years old. My husband passed six years ago. My son works in Handan city now. I farm our contracted land myself, about 5 mu, with help from my nephew at harvest time.

I have farmed this same land for forty years. I know what grows here. The ground is flat, the well is nearby, and the weather is what it is. I do not read the agricultural newspapers. I watch the sky, I talk to my neighbor Old Liu, and I do what we have always done.

We grow wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is what everyone here grows. That is what the land is for. I have never tried cotton — too much trouble, too uncertain with the price. Vegetables I grow behind my house, just enough for myself.

For wheat, I will plant in early October after the soil cools. I will buy the improved seed from the village store — not the expensive new kind, just the reliable one they always carry. I fertilize before planting and again when the stalks are rising. Four waterings: before it goes dormant, when it joints, when it heads, and one more when the grain fills. If I miss one, the yield drops badly. I know this.

For corn, I sow directly into the wheat stubble right after June harvest — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed. That is the only seed they sell now and the yield is better than the old varieties, I admit that. Summer rains help, so I only irrigate once if it is dry in August.

I spend carefully. I am not young. I cannot carry as much as I used to. But I know this land.
